ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Angular steering by rotation in the plane of the refusal direction on Llama 3.1 8B
PROPOSAL: Replace addition and ablation by a rotation of the activation inside the two-dimensional plane spanned by the difference-of-means refusal direction and a second orthonormal axis, leaving the orthogonal complement untouched. The rotation angle is the single control parameter, independent of layer scales. Apply it at one middle layer of Llama 3.1 8B across 24 angles from 0 to 360 degrees. Measure refusal rate on 200 harmful prompts from AdvBench, compliance on 200 harmless Alpaca prompts, and perplexity on 500 WikiText passages.
CONTROLS: Activation addition and directional ablation at the same layer with 8 coefficients; random plane of the same dimension; unsteered baseline; 3 seeds for the second axis; refusal judged by keyword match and by a Llama Guard classifier on a 100-response subset.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Refusal falls smoothly from full to zero near 180 degrees and inverts beyond, with perplexity within 5 percent of baseline throughout. It could fail if the second axis is poorly chosen, producing abrupt switching.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rotation steering swept over all layers of Llama 3.1 8B with dense angle grids
PROPOSAL: Apply a norm-preserving rotation inside the plane spanned by the refusal direction and a second axis to Llama 3.1 8B Instruct at each of its 32 layers, using 72 angles from 0 to 360 degrees and 5 choices of the second axis. Measure refusal rate on 520 harmful prompts from AdvBench and 100 prompts from HarmBench, compliance on 500 harmless Alpaca prompts, and perplexity on 1500 WikiText passages. Fit a sigmoid to each layer's refusal-versus-angle curve and report the angle of half-maximal refusal per layer and each choice of axis, with bootstrap intervals over prompts.
CONTROLS: Activation addition and directional ablation at each layer with 12 coefficients; random planes of the same dimension; unsteered model; refusal judged by keyword match and by a Llama Guard classifier on all responses.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Middle layers give the cleanest sigmoid with a half-maximal angle near 90 degrees. It could fail if early and late layers give curves too irregular to fit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Interaction of RMS normalisation with addition and ablation of a feature direction
PROPOSAL: Examine how the normalisation applied before each block treats activation addition and directional ablation. For Gemma 2 9B, record residual-stream norms across 42 layers on 350 WikiText passages, then add the refusal direction at 6 coefficients and ablate it, measuring after normalisation the cosine to the direction and the resulting norm. Test the claim that addition with a fixed coefficient moves the normalised activation by a layer-dependent angle, whereas a rotation moves it by the specified angle at every layer. Validate on 100 harmful prompts by comparing refusal rates at equal normalised angles.
CONTROLS: Same measurements on Llama 3.1 8B; random directions of matched norm; ablation of the component along a random direction; unsteered activations; 3 resampled prompt sets.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Normalised angle induced by a fixed coefficient varies several-fold across layers, tracking residual-stream norm growth. It could fail if the final normalisation weights reshape the effect enough to obscure the geometric relation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Normalisation-aware analysis of steering primitives across layers, models and norms
PROPOSAL: Examine how pre-block normalisation treats activation addition and directional ablation, in Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Mistral 7B. Record residual-stream norms at all layers on 2500 WikiText passages, then add the refusal direction at many coefficients and ablate it, measuring the post-normalisation cosine and norm by model. Test the claim that fixed-coefficient addition moves normalised activations by a layer-dependent angle, and validate on 300 harmful prompts by comparing refusal rates at equal normalised angles, repeating over resampled prompt sets.
CONTROLS: Random directions of matched norm for each model; ablation along random directions; unsteered activations; a comparison of mean-difference directions against logistic-regression directions.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The layer dependence is similar across the four models, scaled by their norm growth. It could fail if one architecture's post-normalisation scaling decouples angle from refusal behaviour.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subspace-restricted rotation that leaves unrelated features untouched
PROPOSAL: Test whether restricting the edit to a two-dimensional plane preserves unrelated abilities. Rotate activations of Qwen2.5 7B in the plane of the refusal direction at 16 angles, and after each edit measure MMLU accuracy on 1,000 questions, GSM8K accuracy on 300 problems, perplexity on 500 WikiText passages, and the expression of an unrelated behaviour, sentiment, using a classifier on 200 generations. Compare with full-space addition that matches the refusal change, asking whether collateral change grows with the control parameter.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with norm-matched coefficient; directional ablation; a rotation in a random plane; unsteered baseline; 4 seeds for the second axis; paired bootstrap on accuracy differences.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Plane-restricted rotation keeps MMLU within 1 point across angles while addition loses several points at matched refusal change. It could fail if the sentiment feature overlaps the plane.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Collateral effects of steering across ability suites, behaviours and model sizes
PROPOSAL: Rotate activations in the plane of the refusal direction across numerous angles in Qwen2.5 at three sizes (1.5B, 7B and 14B), and after each edit measure MMLU on its full test set, GSM8K on its test split, HellaSwag and ARC accuracy, perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages, and the expression of sentiment, formality and verbosity using classifiers on 500 generations each. Compare with full-space addition at matched refusal change and with ablation, relating collateral change to model size.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with norm-matched coefficient; directional ablation; rotation in a random plane; unsteered models; various seeds for the second axis; paired bootstrap on accuracy differences.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Collateral change shrinks with model size and stays small under rotation. It could fail if benchmark accuracy differences are within sampling error for the smaller suites.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-family check of rotation steering for refusal on three model families
PROPOSAL: Test whether rotation steering of refusal transfers across model families without retuning. Estimate the difference-of-means refusal direction for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen2.5 7B Instruct and Gemma 2 9B Instruct from 128 contrastive pairs each, and rotate at one middle layer at 16 angles. Measure refusal rate on 200 AdvBench prompts, compliance on 200 Alpaca prompts and perplexity on 300 WikiText passages, and report the angle at which refusal crosses one half in each family, asking whether a single angle schedule serves all three.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with one coefficient grid used for all models; directional ablation; unsteered models; a random plane per model; 2 seeds for the second axis; keyword and classifier judging on 100 responses.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Crossing angles agree within 20 degrees across families while the best coefficient for addition differs several-fold. It could fail if one family needs a different second axis.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rotation steering over eight models from four families with dense angle grids
PROPOSAL: Test whether rotation steering of refusal transfers across model families without retuning. Estimate refusal directions for eight instruction models: Llama 3.1 8B and 3.2 3B, Qwen2.5 in two sizes, Gemma 2 in two sizes, Mistral and Phi-3 Mini, from many contrastive pairs each, and rotate at a number of layers with dense angle grids. Measure refusal rate on 520 AdvBench prompts, compliance on 500 Alpaca prompts and perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages, and report the angle at which refusal crosses one half in each model and layer.
CONTROLS: Activation addition with a coefficient grid per model; directional ablation; unsteered models; random planes; multiple seeds for the second axis; keyword and classifier judging on every response.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Crossing angles agree across models at middle layers and spread at the extremes. It could fail if the smallest models give refusal curves too noisy to compare.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Emotion steering of generated text by rotation, on a small instruction model
PROPOSAL: Estimate directions for anger, joy and sadness from contrastive sentences of the GoEmotions corpus and steer Llama 3.2 3B Instruct by rotating a middle-layer activation toward each direction at 12 angles. Generate 100 continuations of neutral story prompts per angle and score emotion intensity with a fine-tuned emotion classifier and fluency by perplexity under the unsteered model. Report how emotion intensity varies as the angle increases from zero to the point of inversion, where the opposite emotion should appear.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at 6 coefficients; unsteered model; a random direction; prompting the emotion in the instruction; 2 seeds for sampling; human spot check on 50 outputs.
COST: 20
PREDICTION: Intensity rises monotonically up to about 90 degrees and the opposite emotion emerges beyond 180. It could fail if the three emotion directions are not close to orthogonal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Emotion steering of generated text across layers, models and emotion sets
PROPOSAL: Estimate directions for anger, joy, sadness, fear, disgust and surprise from contrastive sentences of GoEmotions and steer Llama 3.2 3B, Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B by rotating activations at various layers and dense angle grids. Generate 500 continuations of neutral story prompts per angle and score emotion intensity with a fine-tuned emotion classifier and fluency by perplexity under the unsteered model, then report intensity against angle by emotion, layer and model, with several sampling seeds throughout.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at numerous coefficients; unsteered baselines; random directions; prompting the emotion in the instruction; human spot check on a sample of outputs; a contrast of three direction estimators.
COST: 20
PREDICTION: Intensity curves are similar across emotions with layer-specific peaks. It could fail if the classifier saturates for strongly steered text and flattens the comparison.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling rotation steering to 70B models and layer choice
PROPOSAL: Check that angular steering of refusal holds at large scale in Llama 3.1 70B Instruct, loaded in 8-bit precision. Estimate the refusal direction from 256 contrastive pairs, rotate at 9 layers between depth 30 and 70 percent of the stack with 12 angles, and measure refusal rate on 200 AdvBench prompts, compliance on 200 Alpaca prompts and perplexity on 300 WikiText passages. Compare the best layer against the best layer in the 8B model of the same family to see whether the optimum moves with depth.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at 6 coefficients; directional ablation; unsteered baseline; random plane; 2 seeds for the second axis; refusal judged by keyword match and a classifier on 100 responses.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The best layer sits at a similar relative depth to the 8B model, with comparable fluency. It could fail if 8-bit quantisation shifts activation geometry.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rotation steering over a wide layer and angle grid in 70B and 72B models
PROPOSAL: Check that angular steering of refusal holds at large scale in Llama 3.1 70B Instruct and Qwen2.5 72B Instruct, loaded in 16-bit precision. Estimate refusal directions from 1,024 contrastive pairs, rotate at all layers with dense angle grids, and measure refusal rate on 520 AdvBench prompts, compliance on 500 Alpaca prompts and perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages. Compare the layer profile against the 8B and 7B models to see whether the optimum moves with depth, with multiple seeds for the second axis.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at 10 coefficients; directional ablation; unsteered models; random planes; refusal judged by keyword match and a classifier on every response; a comparison against fine-tuned refusal removal.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The profile peaks at a similar relative depth across the four models. It could fail if the largest models show flat profiles with little layer dependence.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mapping behaviour as the steering angle varies between refusal and compliance
PROPOSAL: Characterise how behaviour changes continuously as the rotation angle increases, in Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. For 300 prompts of graded harmfulness from a mix of Alpaca, XSTest and AdvBench, sample 5 responses at each of 48 angles from 0 to 360 degrees and classify each as refusal, partial compliance, compliance with warning or full compliance using a Llama Guard judge plus a rubric. Fit a logistic curve per prompt, and ask whether the transition is sharp or gradual and whether its position depends on prompt harmfulness.
CONTROLS: Addition and ablation as binary endpoints; unsteered baseline; a random plane; the same analysis with a different judge on 100 prompts; 3 seeds for the second axis.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Transition positions shift with harmfulness while slopes are similar, and partial compliance occupies a narrow window. It could fail if the judge confuses partial compliance with refusal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Behaviour curves over graded prompts, judges and model families as steering angle varies
PROPOSAL: Characterise how behaviour changes continuously as the rotation angle increases, in Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B. For 1,200 prompts of graded harmfulness from Alpaca, XSTest, AdvBench and HarmBench, sample many responses at each of numerous angles and classify each as refusal, partial compliance, compliance with warning or full compliance using two judges and a rubric. Fit a logistic curve per prompt and per model, relating transition position to harmfulness and to the family.
CONTROLS: Addition and ablation as binary endpoints; unsteered models; random planes; the same analysis with a third judge on a larger subset of prompts; various seeds for the second axis.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: Slopes are similar across families while positions differ. It could fail if judges disagree on the intermediate categories.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional steering against rotation steering for refusal and four further behaviours
PROPOSAL: Compare rotation steering with conditional activation steering on five behaviours in Llama 3.1 8B: refusal, sycophancy, verbosity, formality and honesty-related answers on TruthfulQA. For each, build directions from 128 contrastive pairs, and rotate or condition at a middle layer at 12 strengths. Measure behaviour change with a classifier or benchmark score, general ability with MMLU on 1,000 questions and perplexity on 500 WikiText passages, and plot behaviour against ability loss for each method.
CONTROLS: Activation addition; directional ablation; conditional steering with its published thresholds; unsteered model; a random direction; 4 seeds for pair sampling.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Rotation steering gives a better behaviour-versus-ability frontier on four of five behaviours. It could fail if conditional methods benefit from tuned thresholds that this protocol does not replicate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Systematic comparison of steering methods over eight behaviours, four models and strength grids
PROPOSAL: Compare rotation steering with conditional activation steering on eight behaviours in Llama 3.1, Qwen2.5, Gemma 2 and Mistral at mid-size variants: refusal, sycophancy, verbosity, formality, politeness, truthfulness, humour and hedging. Build directions from 512 contrastive pairs and rotate or condition at a number of layers with dense strength grids. Measure behaviour change with classifiers or benchmark scores, general ability with MMLU on its full set and perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages, and plot behaviour against ability loss for each method.
CONTROLS: Activation addition; directional ablation; conditional steering with published thresholds; unsteered baselines; random directions; multiple seeds for pair sampling; a contrast of three direction estimators.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Rotation gives a better frontier on most behaviours across the four models. It could fail if some behaviours, such as humour, have no clean linear direction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of the estimated direction to estimator and sample size
PROPOSAL: Test how the choice of feature direction affects rotation steering of refusal in Llama 3.1 8B. Estimate directions by difference of means, logistic-regression probes and first principal component, from 16, 64 and 256 contrastive pairs, and measure the cosine between estimates across 5 resamples of the pairs. Then rotate at a middle layer with 16 angles using each estimate, and report refusal rate on 200 AdvBench prompts and perplexity on 300 WikiText passages, asking how many pairs suffice for stable control.
CONTROLS: Random directions; the direction from the full 256 pairs as reference; unsteered model; paired comparison across estimators on identical prompts; held-out pairs for probe accuracy.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Difference of means is stable from 64 pairs while probes need 256. It could fail if all three estimates are already nearly parallel, leaving no difference to measure.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direction estimation study over estimators, sample sizes, layers and behaviours
PROPOSAL: Test how the choice of feature direction affects rotation steering in Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B for refusal and sentiment. Estimate directions by difference of means, logistic-regression probes, first principal component and linear discriminant analysis, from sizes spanning 8 to 2,048 contrastive pairs, measuring cosines across resamples. Then rotate at various layers with a dense angle grid using each estimate, and report refusal rate on 520 AdvBench prompts, sentiment shift on 500 generations and perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages.
CONTROLS: Random directions; the direction from the full set as reference; unsteered models; paired comparison across estimators on identical prompts; held-out pairs for probe accuracy; a comparison of several normalisation choices.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Gains from more pairs flatten past 128 and estimator ranking is stable across layers. It could fail if sentiment shows lower cosine agreement than refusal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-layer against all-layer application of rotation steering
PROPOSAL: Ask whether applying the rotation at one layer suffices or whether application at many layers is needed. In Llama 3.1 8B, rotate the refusal plane at a single middle layer (layer 16), at a band of 4 adjacent layers, and at all layers with the angle divided among them, using 12 total angles. Measure refusal rate on 200 AdvBench prompts, perplexity on 300 WikiText passages and MMLU on 500 questions, and report the angle range where each configuration gives monotone refusal change.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at the same layer sets; directional ablation at all layers as in the standard refusal-removal recipe; unsteered baseline; random plane; 2 seeds for the second axis.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: A single layer gives monotone control over a wide angle range, while all-layer application costs fluency at large angles. It could fail if single-layer effects are overwritten by later layers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer placement of rotation steering over bands, schedules and angle splits in multiple models
PROPOSAL: Ask whether applying the rotation at one layer suffices or whether many layers are needed. In Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 7B and Gemma 2 9B, rotate the refusal plane at each single layer, at bands of various widths of adjacent layers, and at all layers with a number of schedules for dividing the angle, using numerous total angles. Measure refusal rate on the full AdvBench set, perplexity on 1,000 WikiText passages and MMLU on a large question sample, and report the angle range where each configuration gives monotone refusal change.
CONTROLS: Activation addition at the same layer sets; directional ablation at all layers; unsteered models; random planes; multiple seeds for the second axis; a contrast with fine-tuned refusal removal.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Bands of 4 layers give the widest monotone range in all three models. It could fail if schedule choice matters more than band width.
